problem.statement: Find a general algebraic formula in radicals that solves every quintic (degree-5) polynomial equation, the way the quadratic formula solves degree 2.

approach.summary: Seek a closed-form radical expression for the roots of the general fifth-degree polynomial.

failure.point: The general quintic's Galois group is the symmetric group S5, which is not solvable; solvability by radicals requires a solvable Galois group, so no such general formula exists.
failure.evidence: Abel–Ruffini theorem (Ruffini 1799; Abel 1824), explained by Galois theory; a standard graduate-algebra result.

environment.description: General polynomials of degree ≥ 5 over the rationals.

transferability.notes: Applies to a general radical formula for degree ≥ 5. Particular quintics with solvable Galois groups are solvable by radicals, and numerical or elliptic methods solve any quintic — just not by radicals in general.
